Direct answers

18 guides

Key Article 50 questions, answered with sources and next steps.

AI answering phone calls: does Article 50 cover voice AI?

Yes.

Can I put ChatGPT (or any custom GPT) on my website in the EU?

Yes — but from 2 August 2026 you must tell visitors they're interacting with AI, clearly and at first contact.

Do I need to disclose AI in customer service (chat, email, voice)?

Chat and voice: yes, clearly — Article 50(1) covers direct AI interaction.

Does my chatbot need to say it's an AI?

Yes — clearly, and before the conversation starts.

Does the EU AI Act apply to UK companies after Brexit?

Yes, whenever their AI interactions or content reach EU users.

Does the EU AI Act apply to US (non-EU) companies?

Yes, if their AI systems or AI-generated content reach people in the EU.

EU AI Act deadlines 2026–2028: the dates that matter

Article 50 transparency rules apply from 2 August 2026 — on schedule.

EU AI Act fines: how much can Article 50 violations cost?

Article 50 infringements can attract fines up to €15 million or 3% of worldwide annual turnover, subject to the AI Act’s rules for undertakings and SMEs.

EU AI Act vs GDPR: what's the difference for my website?

GDPR governs personal data (what you collect and why).

EU AI Act website checklist: 8 things to do before 2 August 2026

Inventory AI systems, establish provider and deployer roles, implement the relevant disclosures, keep proportionate evidence, and set a review date.

How to label AI-generated images correctly (EU AI Act)

Add a visible, unambiguous notice on or next to the image — the EU's standard AI icon or clear text like 'Image generated by AI'.

Is there an EU AI Act exemption for small businesses?

No.

The December 2, 2026 grace period: what it covers (and what it doesn't)

Only one thing: machine-readable marking of AI-generated content for generative AI systems already on the market before 2 August 2026.

The Digital Omnibus delay: what actually changed (the two-clock trap)

The Digital Omnibus (agreed May 2026) delayed high-risk AI Act obligations to December 2027 and August 2028 — but explicitly left Article 50 transparency rules on schedule for 2 August 2026.

The human-review exemption for AI text: what actually qualifies?

AI-generated public-interest text skips the AI label only if a human editor genuinely reviewed it, edited it where needed, and takes editorial responsibility — documented.

What changes on 2 August 2026 for a normal business website?

Four transparency duties switch on: chatbots must say they're AI, deepfakes must be visibly labeled, AI-generated public text must be tagged (unless genuinely human-reviewed), and emotion/biometric system use must be disclosed.

What counts as a deepfake under the EU AI Act?

Any AI-generated or AI-altered audio, image or video that resembles real people, places or events and could pass as authentic.

Who enforces the EU AI Act — and how will they find me?

National market-surveillance authorities in each member state enforce Article 50, coordinated by the EU AI Office.

Glossary

10 guides

Understand the terms used in the regulation and guidance.

AI Office (European Commission) — AI Act glossary

The Commission body coordinating AI Act enforcement across the EU — handling GPAI oversight and guiding national market-surveillance authorities that enforce Article 50 locally.

Conformity assessment — AI Act glossary

The formal evaluation high-risk AI systems must pass to prove they meet AI Act requirements — documentation, testing, sometimes a notified body.

Deepfake (AI Act definition) — AI Act glossary

AI-generated or manipulated audio, image or video content that resembles real persons, objects, places or events and would falsely appear authentic or truthful (Art.

Deployer (AI Act) — AI Act glossary

The person or company using an AI system under their own authority — e.

Emotion recognition system — AI Act glossary

AI that infers emotions or intentions from biometric data (face, voice, posture).

General-purpose AI (GPAI) — AI Act glossary

AI models trained on broad data that can perform many different tasks — ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and friends.

High-risk AI system — AI Act glossary

AI used in sensitive areas listed in Annex III — recruitment, credit scoring, critical infrastructure, education, law enforcement and similar.

Machine-readable marking — AI Act glossary

Technical metadata embedded in AI-generated content (watermarks, C2PA-style provenance) that lets machines detect AI origin.

Provider (AI Act) — AI Act glossary

The company that develops an AI system or has it developed and places it on the market under its own name — e.

Transparency obligation (Article 50) — AI Act glossary

The AI Act's honesty requirement: people must know when they interact with AI, when content is AI-generated, when media is synthetic, and when emotion/biometric systems are used on them.
